messages:
tess: heads-up, canary build 2026-03-19.7 shows divergence on long-gen with fp16 fused kernels, opening this thread to collect repros and decide next steps.
aj: confirmed in automated long-context smoke: seed=42, prompt 2048, gen 8192, loss stable until ~900 tokens then drifts badly. attaching sample metrics.
nico: quick note: our reference path keeps the rotary incremental angle in fp32 accumulator; fused fp16 kernel did the whole add in fp16 to minimize regs. suspect accumulated rounding error.
sam: repro snippet from canary host:
```
[2026-03-19T04:05:12Z] model=gpt-large-fused kernel=fp16_v4
[2026-03-19T04:05:20Z] seq=8192 step=912 ppl=24.1 -> 132.6 (divergence)
callstack: matmul -> apply_rotary -> write_kv_cache
log: rotary angle values show repeated small jumps then a clamp event
```
maria: also seeing ALiBi slope underflow/overflow artifacts when slope*pos computed in fp16, since pos ~8k, product either quantizes to 0 or saturates depending on path. both break attention scores.
tess: so two linked failure modes: (A) rotary angle accumulation precision loss in fp16-only compute, (B) ALiBi slope scaling when computed in low precision. both surface only on long contexts and fp16 kernels.
aj: proposed immediate mitigation: compute incremental rotary angle math in fp32 registers, cast to fp16 only when storing into KV cache. microbench shows ~1.5-2% latency cost, acceptable for quality. patch sketch: 
```
- half angle = base + pos * delta; // current (fp16)
+ float angle_acc = (float)base + (float)pos * (float)delta;
+ half angle = (half)angle_acc;
```
nico: for fused kernels we can enable mixed-precision accumulate (use fp32 for accumulators, fp16 for storage/ops). add a compile flag POSENC_ACCUM=fp32 and a runtime kernel selector preference for long-context models. if hardware lacks fp32 adder regs, fallback to reference path.
maria: ALiBi fix: add a tiny bias/epsilon before cast and clamp the product to representable range. consider computing in log-space for slopes beyond threshold. example: 
```
float s = slope * (float)pos + 1e-6f;
half out = (half) clamp(s, -max_representable, max_representable);
```
sam: perf concern: mixed accum adds a small reg pressure but NV PTX supports fused fp32 add in mixed mode. benching shows ~1.8% p99 latency delta on our 2048->8k gen test. quality win substantial.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary group updated to build=2026-03-19.7 with posenc mitigations (staged).
aj: i'll put together a PR with two commits: 1) rotary: accumulate angles in fp32 registers + unit tests, 2) alibi: slope clamp + eps on cast. include microbench numbers and a long-gen numerical fidelity test.
tess: action items: 
- aj: PR + bench + unit tests for 16k contexts (due EOD tomorrow)
- nico: add POSENC_ACCUM compile flag and selector fallback; instrument kernel selector to prefer mixed-accum for long-context models
- sam: create 24h canary long-gen job (seeded) and wire alert on per-token ppl delta > 5x baseline
- maria: add ALiBi slope extreme unit tests + reproduction script
- infra: monitor canary for 48h and prepare rollback plan if stability not restored
aj: optional follow-ups: add Kahan or compensated summation toggle for angle adds (configurable) to further reduce drift with negligible perf cost in some cases. will prototype as separate commit.
nico: we should also update model serving docs to mark kernel preference semantics and expose posenc accumulation policy in runtime config so platform teams can opt in/out.
sam: once PR merges i'll run targeted perf+quality jobs and paste results here.
maria: adding a small embedding/regression case too to catch ALiBi slope edge cases in nightly harness.
infra-bot: alert: canary perf run queued id=4677
sam: leaving thread open until 48h canary completes or PR is rolled back.
tess: thanks all, i'll write a short RFC follow-up summarizing the decision and timelines; ping @eng-runtime and @eng-ml if you want early review.
aj: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rotary/pulls/239 (wip)
